recoveryCodesRemaining.description: Unspent recovery codes left after the one this sign-in used. Zero is a real answer: the operator should issue a new set before they need one.

recoveryCode.description: One unused recovery code, as printed or retyped — hyphens and letter case do not matter.

idno.description: The organization’s IDNO. Null until its profile records one.

registeredAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the organization was registered on the platform.

entityCount.description: Active reporting entities. An archived entity is not counted.

reportCount.description: Reports the organization holds, in any status — a count only. What a report contains, its stage and its findings are report content and are not published here.

lastSignInAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds of the most recent sign-in by any active member. Null when no member has signed in.

id.description: The account’s id, or the invitation’s — `kind` says which, and so which routes act on it.

role.description: The realm — fixed when the invitation was sent, never changed afterwards.

standing.description: One word read from the facts: an account is active, locked (active and locked out after repeated failures), suspended or removed; an invitation is invited, or lapsed once its link has expired.

lastSignInAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds of the most recent sign-in. Null for an invitation, and for an account that has never signed in.

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds after which an invitation’s link stops working. Null for an account.

supportAccessRequests.description: Support-access requests the account raised in the last 30 days, whatever became of them (task 67.9). Null for an invitation.

id.description: Identifies the invitation for a resend or a revoke.

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds after which the link stops working — 24 hours after sending.

email.description: The operator’s address. The link goes here, and the account it creates holds this address.

role.description: The realm the account will belong to. The two realms are separate accounts: a realm is not changed later.

email.description: The address the account will hold.

role.description: The realm the account will belong to.

expiresAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds after which the link stops working.

token.description: The single-use value from the invitation link.

secret.description: The base32 secret, for typing into an authenticator that cannot scan.

uri.description: The otpauth Key Uri the enrolment symbol encodes — the same secret, scannable.

email.description: The address to sign in with.

token.description: The single-use value from the invitation link.

password.description: The operator’s password, under the same policy as every other: minimum 8 and maximum 128 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one further character.

totpCode.description: A current code from the authenticator the enrolment secret was entered into. The account exists only once this confirms.

occurredAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when it happened.

actorId.description: The operator who acted. Null for the provisioning command, and for a sign-in attempt against an address that matches no account.

actorEmail.description: The acting operator’s address. Null with `actorId`, or where no account holds that id.

targetId.description: The account, invitation or provider configuration version the event acted on. Null for an event that acted on none.

targetEmail.description: The target’s address, where the target is an account or an invitation.

targetProvider.description: The social provider, where the target is a provider’s configuration version (task 67.11).

recoveryCodesIssuedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, UTC, when the current set of recovery codes was issued. Null until the operator issues a first set — nothing else creates one.

recoveryCodesRemaining.description: Unspent codes of the current set. Zero when every one has been used, and zero when none was ever issued — the issue date tells the two apart.

otherSessionsTerminated.description: How many other sessions were ended. Always 0 when the election was not made, and 0 is a normal answer when it was.

currentPassword.description: The password in force now. A change without the correct one is refused.

password.description: The replacement, under the same policy as every password: minimum 8 and maximum 128 characters, with at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit and one further character.

terminateOtherSessions.description: End the operator’s **other** active sessions. Opt-in, and false when omitted; the session making this request is never one of them.

password.description: The operator’s current password. Every write on this screen asks for it.

code.description: A current code from the authenticator the staged secret was entered into.

recoveryCodes.description: Ten single-use codes, shown exactly once. Every code of an earlier set stopped working when these were issued.

enabled.description: Whether sign-in, registration and linking through the provider are offered. Changed only by the enablement and disablement routes, never by a configuration save.

clientId.description: The client ID the provider issued; empty until the provider is registered.

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer discovery runs against; empty until the provider is configured.

scopes.description: The scopes requested — the three FR-2 names, not editable here.

redirectUris.description: The exact redirect addresses a sign-in may return to.

revision.description: The configuration revision in force, sent back with a change so that a newer one refuses it. 0 before anything was published for the provider.

enablementBlocker.description: The first reason the provider could not sign anyone in — no client ID, no redirect address, or no client secret held — or null when it could. Set for an enabled provider too, whose secret may since have left the environment.

secretHeld.description: Whether the server holds the provider’s client secret. Never the secret itself.

secretSetting.description: The environment variable that holds the client secret — where it is set, since this surface cannot set it. A change to it takes effect when the server restarts.

linkedAccounts.description: Accounts holding an identity through the provider.

accountsWithoutOtherCredential.description: Of those, the accounts with no password and no other provider — which, once the provider is disabled, sign in again only by resetting their password.

changedByEmail.description: The operator who published the configuration in force. Null for a seeded configuration.

changedAt.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the configuration in force was published.

id.description: The configuration version now in force.

revision.description: Its revision — what the next change is made against.

clientId.description: The client ID the provider issued. Saving the first one registers the provider; saving another rotates it. May be empty while the provider is disabled.

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer discovery runs against — a complete https address with no query or fragment.

redirectUris.description: The exact redirect addresses a sign-in may return to, each ending in `/auth/social/{provider}/callback`. Blank entries and repeats are dropped. May be empty while the provider is disabled.

revision.description: The revision this change was made against — the one the reading answered. A newer one in force refuses the change (problem type identity-provider-changed).
